title: Files, Folders, File Extensions and Paths
learningObjectives: Explain how files and folders organize a project
Identify a file extension and describe what it can and cannot tell you
Read simple folder trees and distinguish relative paths from absolute paths
Use safe, clear names and paths when organizing a web project

understand.concept: A file stores information, such as text, an image or program code. A folder (also called a directory) groups files and other folders so a project stays organized. A path describes how to locate a file or folder. A file extension is the ending of a filename, commonly used by systems and applications as a clue about its format or intended handling.
understand.whyItMatters: Web projects quickly contain HTML pages, CSS stylesheets, JavaScript files, images and other resources. Clear folders and correct paths help the browser and developer tools find the right resources and make projects easier to maintain.
understand.history: Early file systems organized information into named files and directories. Extensions became a widely used convention for indicating file types, especially in systems that associate applications with filename endings. Modern systems may also inspect file contents, so an extension alone does not prove a file's actual format.
understand.analogy: Think of a school library: the library is the project, shelves are folders, each book is a file, and a catalogue location is a path. A book's label can hint at its subject, but the label alone does not prove what is inside.
understand.analogyLimit: Digital folders are logical locations, not physical shelves. A path follows exact naming and separator rules, and two files can have the same name when they are in different folders.

explain.narrative: Consider this project tree: my-site/ contains index.html, css/styles.css, js/app.js and images/logo.png. The slash separates folder names in these web-style paths. From the project root, css/styles.css is a relative path: it tells us where to go starting from the current base folder. An absolute path identifies a location from a file-system root or another defined root, and its exact form depends on the operating system. In an HTML file at the project root, href="css/styles.css" points to the stylesheet. In a page inside a subfolder, the relative path may need to change. Names and letter case can matter, especially on web servers. Spaces and unusual characters are best avoided in beginner project filenames; use short descriptive names and hyphens when needed.

examples.code:
my-site/
├── index.html
├── css/
│   └── styles.css
├── js/
│   └── app.js
└── images/
    └── logo.png
examples.explanation: The tree shows one project folder and three resource folders. Each indented item belongs to the folder immediately above it. The path from the project root to the logo is images/logo.png.
examples.expectedOutput: A clear project structure with separate folders for styles, scripts and images.

examples.code: Page:       my-site/index.html\nStylesheet: my-site/css/styles.css\nRelative URL from index.html: css/styles.css
examples.explanation: The browser resolves this relative URL using the document's base URL. It enters the css folder and looks for styles.css. A leading slash or a different document location changes how a path is resolved.
examples.expectedOutput: The page can locate the stylesheet when the file and path match.

practise.guidedTask: Using the project tree above, write the relative path from index.html to app.js and to logo.png. Then explain why css/style.css would fail if the actual filename is styles.css.
practise.independentTask: Draw a folder tree for a small profile website containing one HTML page, one CSS file, one JavaScript file and two images. Write the relative path to each resource from index.html.
hints: Start from the folder containing the page, unless the URL begins with a root-relative slash.
Check every folder name and filename, including spelling and letter case.
An extension is a clue, not a guarantee of file contents.

questions.prompt: From my-site/index.html, which relative path points to my-site/css/styles.css?
questions.explanation: The css folder is a child of the project root, so the path starts with css/.

questions.prompt: What does a file extension tell you?
options: It always proves the exact contents
It is a common clue about a file's format or intended handling
It tells you the file's folder path
questions.answer: It is a common clue about a file's format or intended handling
questions.explanation: Extensions are useful conventions, but a filename can be misleading and systems may inspect file contents.
